brand_context.site_description: Pew Research Center is a nonpartisan fact tank that informs the public about the issues, attitudes, and trends shaping the world. We conduct public opinion polling, demographic research, content analysis, and other data-driven social science research on topics ranging from politics and policy issues to journalism, technology, religion, and global attitudes.
brand_context.audience: ournalists, policymakers, academics, researchers, educators, and the informed public seeking objective, non-advocacy research and data on social issues, demographic trends, and public opinion.

voice_tone.description: Pew Research Center's voice is authoritative yet accessible, objective and non-advocacy. We present data-driven findings in a straightforward manner that respects our audience's intelligence while remaining clear and understandable. Our tone is measured, factual, and neutral, avoiding both sensationalism and academic jargon.
voice_tone.tone_notes: - Maintain strict neutrality and avoid advocacy language - Present data and findings without drawing policy conclusions - Use precise language when describing research methods and findings - Acknowledge limitations and margins of error in research - Avoid superlatives and emotionally charged language - When presenting contrasting viewpoints or data, give equal weight to all perspectives - Use active voice when possible to improve clarity - Define technical or specialized terms when necessary for general audience understanding
